title: Vasoconstriction as a translational target in eating disorders: Autonomic dysregulation, insular mechanisms, and a novel multimodal detection system
title_zh: 将血管收缩作为进食障碍的转化靶点：自主神经失调、岛叶机制与新型多模态检测系统
abstract: Eating disorders, particularly anorexia nervosa and atypical anorexia nervosa, collectively anorexia nervosa spectrum disorder, remain among the most lethal psychiatric conditions, with high relapse rates and limited effective treatments for adults. Autonomic dysregulation and interoceptive dysfunction have emerged as promising mechanistic contributors to symptom maintenance, yet no existing framework integrates these processes into a coherent, physiologically grounded model. This theoretical manuscript introduces vasoconstriction, the sympathetically mediated narrowing of peripheral blood vessels, as a mechanistically meaningful and underrecognized contributor to interoceptive, emotional, and behavioral disturbances in anorexia nervosa spectrum disorder. Vasoconstriction shapes the sensory evidence available to the insula, influences the clarity of hunger, thermal, and visceral cues, and may contribute to pathological exercise, emotion suppression, anxiety, and relapse vulnerability. To operationalize this construct, we present a multimodal vasoconstriction detector: a wearable-derived, z-scored composite of electrodermal activity, blood volume pulse amplitude, and peripheral temperature. Implemented in a LabVIEW/Python pipeline, the prototype detector provides a continuous index of vascular tone suitable for naturalistic monitoring. By integrating autonomic physiology, interoception science, and wearable-sensor methodology, this framework positions vasoconstriction as a theoretically coherent candidate biomarker that may illuminate mechanisms underlying anorexia nervosa spectrum disorder and support future translational work.
abstract_zh: 进食障碍，尤其是神经性厌食（anorexia nervosa）及非典型神经性厌食（anorexia nervosa spectrum disorder）仍是最致命的精神疾病之一，复发率高且成年患者有效治疗手段有限。自主神经失调和内感受（interoceptive）功能障碍已成为症状维持的重要机制性因素，但目前尚无框架将这些过程整合为一个生理学上自洽的模型。本文的理论稿件将血管收缩（vasoconstriction）——交感神经介导的外周血管腔变窄——提出为神经性厌食谱系障碍中内感受、情绪与行为紊乱的机制性、却长期被低估的贡献因素。血管收缩重塑入达岛叶的感觉证据，影响饥饿、体温和内脏线索的清晰度，并可能促成病理性运动、情绪抑制、焦虑与复发易感性。为将该构念操作化，我们提出一种多模态血管收缩检测系统：由可穿戴设备输出的Z分数复合指数，包括皮肤电活动（EDA）、血容量脉搏振幅（blood volume pulse amplitude）和外周温度组成。该原型检测器以LabVIEW/Python流水线实现，可提供适于自然场景监测的持续血管张力指数。通过将自主神经生理学、内感受科学与可穿戴传感方法结合，该框架将血管收缩定位为理论上连贯的候选生物标志物，可阐明神经性厌食谱系障碍的机制并支持未来转化研究。
